definition: Common Criteria Recognition Arrangement — an arrangement under which participating countries plan to recognise Common Criteria (ISO/IEC 15408) certificates authorised by any Certificate Authorising Participant. Only Certificate Authorising Participants authorise certificates issued by their certification bodies; Certificate Consuming Participants recognise them without issuing their own. Recognition covers certificates for evaluations against a collaborative Protection Profile or at EAL 1 to 2 with ALC_FLR.
technicalNote: On the Common Criteria Portal, Certificate Authorising Participants include Australia, Canada, France (ANSSI), Germany (BSI), Japan, the Republic of Korea and the United States (NIAP); the United Kingdom is listed as a Certificate Consuming Participant. Participants plan to recognise certificates only within the arrangement's scope, and a participant may decline to recognise a certificate where recognising it would conflict with its law or, for an application involving classified information, for that application only (Articles 2 and 3). The EU's EUCC is a separate scheme set out in Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/482 and applicable from 27 February 2025: certification bodies issue EUCC certificates at assurance level 'substantial' or 'high', and certification from a third country is recognised within the Union only through a mutual recognition agreement with the Union (Article 44).

definition: National Institute of Standards and Technology, the U.S. agency leading PQC standardization through its Post-Quantum Cryptography project.
European Telecommunications Standards Institute, producing PQC migration guides and standards for European industry.
Internet Engineering Task Force, developing PQC integration into internet protocols like TLS, SSH, and IKEv2.
French National Cybersecurity Agency, publishing PQC recommendations and cryptographic certifications for France and Europe.
German Federal Office for Information Security, providing PQC migration guidelines and recommendations for German government systems.
The partnership project that develops specifications for mobile telecommunications including 5G security architecture.
National Security Agency, the U.S. intelligence agency that publishes CNSA 2.0 and mandates PQC adoption timelines for national security systems.
Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, the U.S. agency coordinating PQC migration for critical infrastructure and publishing product category lists.
European Union Agency for Cybersecurity, publishing PQC guidelines and coordinating quantum-safe transitions across EU member states.
Global System for Mobile Communications Association, leading the Post-Quantum Telco Network Taskforce for PQC integration in mobile networks.
An industry body of Certificate Authorities and browser vendors that governs Web PKI certificate standards, including PQC certificate adoption rules.
UK National Cyber Security Centre, publishing PQC migration guidance and a 2035 deadline for full transition to quantum-safe cryptography.
China's Office of State Commercial Cryptography Administration, managing China's independent cryptographic standards including SM2 and PQC competitions.
Joint Technical Committee 1 of ISO and IEC, the international standards body for information technology including cryptographic standards (SC 27).
The European Quantum Communication Infrastructure initiative, a pan-EU program to deploy a quantum communication network across all 27 member states combining terrestrial fiber and satellite links.

An open-source project (Linux Foundation) for keyless code signing. Developers authenticate with their existing identity (GitHub, Google) and receive short-lived certificates, eliminating long-term key management.
technicalNote: Sigstore uses cryptography in several places: the signing client creates an ephemeral key pair, Fulcio (the certificate authority) issues a short-lived certificate bound to an OpenID Connect identity, Rekor (the transparency log) records the signing event, and a timestamp authority is a further service that uses cryptography. Moving Fulcio and Rekor to ML-DSA would not by itself make downstream consumers post-quantum safe: each signing client, each verifier, the trusted-root and bundle formats, and the verification policy also have to support the new algorithm. The Sigstore project's 2025 plan was to let clients experiment with ML-DSA keys first and to adopt post-quantum algorithms in its public-good services once vetted implementations are available in Go; it lists open questions such as how verification material is signed and how users set verification policy.

definition: Post-Quantum Cryptographic Alliance, a Linux Foundation project bringing together industry and academia to advance PQC adoption through open-source software.
Open Quantum Safe, an open-source project providing C library (liboqs) implementations of post-quantum algorithms and integrations with OpenSSL, BoringSSL, and other libraries.
Australian Signals Directorate, Australia's national cybersecurity agency. Published aggressive PQC migration timelines with a 2030 deadline for full transition — five years ahead of the US.
Canadian Centre for Cyber Security, Canada's technical authority on cybersecurity. Published the ITSM.40.001 PQC migration roadmap for the Government of Canada.
Cryptography Research and Evaluation Committees, Japan's organization for evaluating and recommending cryptographic algorithms for government use.
Korean Post-Quantum Cryptography project, South Korea's national initiative to develop and standardize its own PQC algorithms including HAETAE, AIMer, SMAUG-T, and NTRU+.
International Telecommunication Union — Telecommunication Standardization Sector. Study Group 17 (SG17) is developing PQC standards for telecommunications infrastructure.
NIST National Cybersecurity Center of Excellence, collaborating with industry to develop practical PQC migration guidance and reference architectures.
Bank for International Settlements, the international financial institution that published the quantum-readiness roadmap (Paper 158) for the global financial system.
Chinese Association for Cryptologic Research, the organization that ran China's independent PQC competition and is shaping the NGCC (Next-Generation Commercial Cryptographic) standards program.
The IETF working group responsible for standardizing Merkle Tree Certificates and related post-quantum PKI infrastructure. Adopted draft-ietf-plants-merkle-tree-certs in January 2026.

Cryptographic Module Validation Program — a joint NIST and CCCS program that tests cryptographic modules against FIPS 140-3 requirements. Validated modules appear on the NIST CMVP validated-modules list with a certificate number, recording that an accredited laboratory tested that module version against FIPS 140-3 at the stated security level; the Approved algorithms inside it must first complete CAVP algorithm validation.
technicalNote: Modules containing FIPS 203, 204 or 205 algorithms appear on the CMVP list only after the algorithm implementations have CAVP validation, and validation queue times vary; check the CMVP Modules In Process list. Procurement requiring FIPS 140-3 validated PQC must read the certificate for the exact module version and algorithms. Check: csrc.nist.gov/projects/cmvp.

definition: International standard (ISO/IEC 15408) for security-product evaluation. National schemes (BSI Germany, ANSSI France, NIAP US, the Canadian Common Criteria Scheme, etc.) oversee evaluation and certification; the CCRA lets participants recognise certificates authorised by Certificate Authorising Participants, within its scope (collaborative Protection Profiles, or EAL 1 to 2 with ALC_FLR). In the EU, the EUCC (Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/482, applicable from 27 February 2025) builds on the SOG-IS mutual recognition agreement.

Singapore's national cybersecurity authority. Publishes the Cybersecurity Code of Practice and PQC readiness guidance for critical-information-infrastructure operators. Note: also used for Cloud Security Alliance (separate org).
CCCS Canada's technical-guidance document series (ITSM.40.xxx, ITSAP.xx.xxx). The PQC-relevant entry today is ITSAP.00.017 — Preparing your organization for the quantum threat to cryptography.
Singapore's central bank and integrated financial regulator. Publishes Technology Risk Management Guidelines and circulars that cover cryptographic-control expectations for financial institutions.
South Korea's national agency for cybersecurity and internet governance. Operates the K-CMVP cryptographic-module validation programme and co-administers the KpqC competition with academic partners.
South Korea's policy ministry for science, ICT, and broadcasting. Co-sponsors the KpqC standardization competition with KISA and the National Intelligence Service.

US Department of Defense combat-support agency that runs IT infrastructure for the joint warfighter. Maintains the STIG library that locks down DoD system configurations, including cryptographic-suite controls.

Industry consortium that publishes the TPM (Trusted Platform Module) and DICE (Device Identifier Composition Engine) specifications. PQC-relevant work covers TPM 2.0 PQC algorithm additions and attestation-quote signing.
International Organization for Standardization, a Geneva-based body that develops and publishes international standards.
technicalNote: Develops cryptographic standards jointly with IEC through ISO/IEC JTC 1 (already in this glossary).

definition: International Electrotechnical Commission, the international standards body for electrical and electronic technologies.
technicalNote: Jointly operates ISO/IEC JTC 1 with ISO, the committee responsible for IT security standards including cryptographic techniques.

definition: Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, a professional association that publishes technical standards — including IEEE 1609.2 (vehicular communications) and IEEE 2030.5 (smart grid), both already in this glossary — now being updated for PQC.
Office of Management and Budget, the U.S. executive-branch office that issues implementation guidance directing federal agencies on PQC migration planning and budgeting.
technicalNote: Issued M-23-02 (2022, cryptographic inventories) and M-26-15 (2026, the operative PQC migration schedule under EO 14412), both already in this glossary.

definition: Department of Defense, the U.S. military department that mandates CNSA 2.0 compliance for National Security Systems and drives PQC migration timelines across defense contractors and suppliers.

Organization for the Advancement of Structured Information Standards, a nonprofit consortium that develops open standards — including KMIP, already in this glossary, which now extends to PQC key types.

National Information Assurance Partnership, the U.S. Common Criteria certification body operated jointly by NSA and NIST; issues CC certificates recognized under the CCRA (both already in this glossary).

World Wide Web Consortium, the standards body for web technologies including WebAuthn and Verifiable Credentials, which are incorporating PQC algorithm support for web authentication and digital credentials.

Open Worldwide Application Security Project, a nonprofit foundation producing widely used application-security guidance (e.g. the OWASP Top 10) that is beginning to address crypto-agility and PQC migration risk for software developers.
PCI Security Standards Council, the payment-card-industry body (founded by the major card brands) that maintains PCI DSS and is issuing PQC migration guidance for payments.
A U.S. nonprofit operating federally funded R&D centers, best known in security circles for maintaining the CVE program and the ATT&CK adversary-tactics framework.

An industry association that standardizes secure-element and trusted-execution-environment specifications used in SIM cards, secure elements, and IoT hardware roots of trust, now extending its specifications to PQC-capable secure elements.

A nonprofit industry association publishing cloud-security best practices, distinct from Singapore's Cyber Security Agency (also abbreviated CSA — see that entry). Runs an active Quantum-Safe Security working group producing PQC migration guidance for cloud providers and customers.
